finalText:
I'll run LedgerMind's analysis over your intents.
**Yes — 0.80 USDC is genuinely idle, and it's all in one place.**

**The idle money: 0.80 USDC in `0xe88b02…df16`** ("Marketing tools trial – Q3"). You revoked it with the reason "Trial ended, tool not adopted." You funded it with 1 USDC, the agent spent 0.20 USDC on a single payment to merchant `0x3333…3333`, and the remaining 0.80 USDC is stranded — a revoked intent can never spend again, so that balance will sit there forever.

**What to do:** call `withdrawRemainder` on `0xe88b02…df16`. It returns the full 0.80 USDC to you. Nothing else is needed — no other intent is Revoked or Expired, so this is the entire recoverable pool.

**The bigger issue, though, isn't idle cash — it's idle *authority*.** You've authorised **67 USDC** across 4 intents but only ever spent **1.28 USDC**. Two things worth fixing:

1. **`0x568222…2f5b`** ("General ops agent – discretionary spend") — 10 USDC total / 2 USDC per tx with **no merchant allowlist**, meaning the agent can pay *any* address. It has made zero payments and holds only 0.30 USDC, so the only thing limiting damage right now is thin funding, not the rules. Restrict the allowlist before you top it up — cheap to fix now, expensive later.
2. **`0xb530e9…7ca7`** ("Research paper + dataset subscriptions") — 50 USDC cap against 0.10 USDC of actual spend (0.2% used). Cut the cap toward real subscription size; it removes ~49 USDC of standing authorisation without touching any real payment.

**One anomaly worth a look:** `0x4e0866…bcf4` (cloud infra) made two 0.49 USDC payments **seven seconds apart**, both at 98% of its 0.50 USDC per-tx cap, to the same merchant. That's the signature of one invoice being split to squeeze under the cap. Confirm the real invoice amount, then raise the per-tx cap so charges land as single payments — the allowlist there is already locked to one merchant, so the added risk is contained.

**Caveats on the data:** the analysis covers a 90-day window and found no Expired intents — if you have expired intents older than that, their idle balances aren't counted here. Also, all four payments happened within about a minute on 2026-09-13, so there's no real spending history to size caps against; treat the cap recommendations as directional. Merchant addresses are raw with no names, so I can't tell you who `0x1111…` actually is.

findings.title: Unrestricted merchant allowlist on an unused 10 USDC intent
findings.detail: 0x568222982112b7bd55bd90524e1434472f422f5b ('General ops agent - discretionary spend') authorises 10 USDC total / 2 USDC per tx with merchantAllowlistSize = 0 and unrestrictedMerchants = true. It has made zero payments and holds 0.30 USDC funded. Any merchant on earth is a valid destination for up to 2 USDC per transaction here; the only thing limiting loss today is the thin 0.30 USDC funding, not the authorisation.

findings.title: Cloud infra agent is being throttled at the per-tx cap
findings.detail: 0x4e0866d3c7ac1acbd4058cc9a0877193e640bcf4 made two payments of 0.49 USDC each, both at 98% of the 0.50 USDC perTxCap, to the same merchant 0x1111…1111 seven seconds apart. Back-to-back near-cap payments to one merchant is the classic signature of a single charge being split to fit the cap. The intent has also burned 49% of its 2 USDC total cap on those two transactions alone, so it will exhaust its authorisation quickly at this rate.

findings.title: Research intent is over-authorised by roughly 500x its observed spend
findings.detail: 0xb530e9ca418560028db414e09aa36617a89e7ca7 carries a 50 USDC total cap and 5 USDC per-tx cap but has made one payment of 0.10 USDC (2% of perTxCap) and used 0.2% of its total cap. The allowlist is restricted to one merchant, which contains blast radius, but the headroom is far larger than any demonstrated need.

actions.rationale: Intent is Revoked and the tool was not adopted, so the 0.80 USDC remaining will never be spent against it. This is the only recoverable idle balance in the window; withdrawRemainder returns it in full.

A 10 USDC / 2 USDC-per-tx authorisation with an empty allowlist and zero payment history is open-ended by construction. Pin it to the specific merchants discretionary ops is meant to pay before it is funded further; today only 0.30 USDC sits behind it, so the fix is cheap now and expensive later.

50 USDC authorised against 0.10 USDC observed spend (0.2% cap used). Cutting the total cap toward the scale of actual subscription charges removes ~49 USDC of standing authorisation without affecting any observed payment.

Two consecutive 0.49 USDC payments at 98% of the 0.50 USDC per-tx cap to the same merchant indicate charge splitting, which inflates payment count and obscures true invoice size. Confirm the real invoice amount with the infra merchant, then size perTxCap above it so each charge lands as one payment; this intent's allowlist is already restricted to one merchant, so the added risk is contained.

dataGaps: No Expired intents appear in the 90-day window, so the idle figure reflects revoked capital only — if expired intents exist outside this window they are not counted here.

Funding events and their timestamps are not exposed, so the age of the 0.80 USDC idle balance cannot be derived (idleDays is reported as 0 on the revoked intent, which conflicts with it already being revoked).
Merchant addresses are raw (0x1111…, 0x2222…, 0x3333…) with no names or categories, so allowlist recommendations cannot name the counterparties to pin.
The true invoice amount for the cloud infra merchant is unknown, so the correct replacement perTxCap for 0x4e0866…bcf4 cannot be computed — only that 0.50 USDC appears too low.

All four payments occurred within roughly one minute on a single day (2026-09-13), so there is no cadence history to validate the stated 'weekly' schedule or to establish a spend baseline for cap sizing.
